duplicateVertices.acceptance: exact full-attribute redundancy is zero or materially lower, rendering comparison is unchanged, and topology/watertightness metrics do not regress.

collisionRootCause.whyAnyCollisionAtAll721Angles: The sparse frozen scanner reports internal containment for all block pairs, but the independent surface test also confirms crankshaft/block triangle intersection at all 721 angles. Therefore the assembly-wide 721/721 failure is not removable as a false positive.
collisionRootCause.why107MmIsNotDepth: It is the greatest nearest-outer-triangle distance among a few sampled points classified inside the outer closed block surface. It is not an overlap depth between two closed material volumes.
collisionRootCause.why21413884MmIsNotDepth: It is radial excess beyond the liner centerline radius for sampled rod vertices inside the liner axial span. It neither follows the liner surface normal nor computes a material-volume overlap.
collisionRootCause.confirmedDefect: The block is a closed exterior ExtrudeGeometry without four bores or a crankcase void, and each liner is an unrelieved open cylinder. Blender surface triangles confirm resulting intersections.

roles.counterweightWeb: 8/8 nodes reached but only parent-level pair reported

samplingCoverage.timingAndAccessoryGap: The timing chain is exported under camshaft and the accessory belt under cooling-system, neither of which is in the frozen dynamic-parts scan. The timing crank sprocket's 19 nodes receive zero aggregate sample points. Unrelated-shell clearance is therefore unmeasured, not passed.
samplingCoverage.acceptance: Scan every crank semantic node or explicit role, report the responsible subpart, cover 44/44 crank nodes including 19/19 sprocket nodes, and include timing chain/accessory belt/pulley versus unrelated shells.

findings.title: Block, crankcase and liners have confirmed moving-surface intersections
findings.qualityImpact: The visible motion can be mechanically legible while the exported solid geometry remains physically contradictory.
findings.expectedBenefit: Restores defensible non-interference for the core motion chain and removes the largest external-evaluation weakness.
findings.risk: Changing block/liner topology may reduce the silhouette, watertightness, section readability or frame rate.
findings.acceptance: 721-angle Blender triangle scan reports zero unclassified moving-part/block and rod/liner surface intersections; no new whitelist entries are used.

findings.title: Sixteen cam lobes have reversed cap boundary winding
findings.qualityImpact: Normals and face orientation are internally inconsistent even though the meshes remain closed.
findings.expectedBenefit: Zeroes a deterministic cross-tool topology defect with a two-index-order correction.
findings.risk: A wrong one-sided correction can invert a cap or total signed volume.
findings.acceptance: Both tools report 0 winding errors, 0 invalid normals and 16/16 lobes remain watertight with positive volume.

findings.title: Frozen collision sampling cannot attribute or cover crank/timing subparts
findings.qualityImpact: Counterweight, journal, sprocket, chain and belt clearance cannot be independently defended.
findings.expectedBenefit: Turns an aggregate alarm into actionable part-level mechanical evidence and closes explicit coverage gaps.
findings.risk: A broader scan can be slower and can expose more true issues; that is evidence, not a reason to suppress it.
findings.acceptance: All semantic crank/timing/accessory roles are enumerated and unrelated-shell pairs are checked over their motion cycles.

findings.title: Only one third of coincident vertices are exact observed-attribute redundancy
findings.qualityImpact: The original 51% headline overstates safe optimization; blind welding would damage hard edges and UV seams.
findings.expectedBenefit: A full-attribute indexing pass can remove up to 16,876 vertices (16.76% of raw) without intentionally changing appearance.
findings.risk: Ignoring tangents, colors, skinning or future attributes can still alter rendering.
findings.acceptance: Full-attribute redundancy falls without changing normal/UV seams, material primitives, topology metrics or matched screenshots.

findings.title: Frozen penetration magnitudes are proxy distances, not physical depths
findings.qualityImpact: Calling 107 mm or 21.413884 mm penetration depth would overstate what was measured.
findings.expectedBenefit: Reports become technically defensible while retaining the real collision failures.
findings.risk: None if raw values remain preserved and relabeled.
findings.acceptance: Reports label both metrics as proxies and pair them with triangle-overlap angle ranges; no proxy is presented as physical overlap depth.

explicitNonImplementations: Do not whitelist block, liner, timing or accessory intersections to improve the score.
Do not position-weld all 51% coincident vertices; 67.26% of the duplicate count is required by observed normal or UV seams.
Do not chase the 28-vertex Blender/Trimesh importer-count difference: both tools agree on every scored topology conclusion.
Do not shrink or hide rods, pistons, crankshaft, block or liners to avoid intersections; derive any liner relief or cavity from the 720-degree swept envelope and an explicit clearance.
Do not treat timing/accessory pairs as passed until coverage exists.

scoreOpinion.reason: Classification corrects the interpretation of proxy depths but independent triangle overlap still supports a zero collision subscore.
